name: United States — Federal (+ multi-state)
summary: Employment is at-will under a federal floor (Title VII, ADA, ADEA, PWFA, FLSA, FMLA, NLRA, ERISA/ACA) layered with fast-diverging state and city law, so a remote engineer's work state, not HQ, drives pay transparency, paid leave, final pay, non-compete, AI-hiring and WARN rules. Federal enforcement priorities swung hard in 2025-26: EEO-1 and EO 11246 affirmative action are being dismantled, DEI programs face EEOC/DOJ and False Claims Act scrutiny, the NLRB now has a Republican majority but Stericycle and McLaren Macomb remain binding, and H-1B policy is volatile (weighted lottery, a $100,000 fee that is vacated but extended, a proposed $103,265 cap fee, and higher proposed prevailing wages). A California-HQ semiconductor employer most often errs by applying California or HQ templates nationwide (or ignoring other states' rules for remote staff), by using broad confidentiality and non-disparagement clauses in severance agreements, by running demographic-targeted DEI programs, and by mixing I-9 verification with export-control screening.

ratingNotes.termination: At-will with no statutory notice or severance, but discrimination/retaliation litigation, OWBPA release rules and WARN/state mini-WARN create real process cost.
ratingNotes.representation: Private-sector union density is low (about 6%), but NLRA Section 7 protects non-union engineers' concerted activity and polices handbook and severance language.
ratingNotes.privacy: No omnibus federal employee-privacy law; risk sits in state laws (IL BIPA, CA CCPA, NY/CT/DE monitoring notices), FCRA, HIPAA and state breach laws.
ratingNotes.payTransparency: No federal range-posting law, but 13 states plus DC and several cities require ranges now (CT joins Oct 1, 2026 and DE in 2027), many reaching remote roles.
ratingNotes.workingTime: FLSA exempt misclassification is the main exposure; several states set higher salary thresholds and daily overtime; OBBBA adds separate W-2 tracking of qualified overtime from 2026.
ratingNotes.leave: No federal paid leave; about 12 state PFML programs plus DC (MD from 2028) and about 19 state paid sick leave laws with different accrual, notice and job-protection rules.
ratingNotes.immigration: H-1B rules changed repeatedly in 2025-26 (weighted lottery, $100K fee litigation, proposed $103,265 cap fee, prevailing wage NPRM, layoffs EO, F-1 fixed-admission rule).
ratingNotes.changeVelocity: 2025-26 brought reversals at EEOC, NLRB, OFCCP and DOL plus OBBBA payroll changes and a steady flow of new state laws each Jan 1 and Jul 1.

keyFacts.label: Employment model
keyFacts.value: At-will in 49 states (Montana requires good cause after probation under its Wrongful Discharge from Employment Act). Either party may end employment at any time for any lawful reason; exceptions are discrimination, retaliation, public-policy discharge and implied or express contract.

keyFacts.label: Contracts & offer letters
keyFacts.value: No written contract required. Use offer letters with at-will disclaimer, exempt/non-exempt status, and contingencies (I-9, background check, IP/confidentiality agreement with DTSA notice). Some states require written wage notices at hire (e.g., NY Labor Law 195.1) or written commission plans (e.g., NY). Arbitration with class waivers is enforceable, but sexual harassment/assault claims cannot be forced into arbitration (EFAA 2022).

keyFacts.label: Probation
keyFacts.value: No statutory probation. Avoid wording like 'permanent after probation' that implies for-cause protection; Montana is the exception (WDEA probation period). Benefits waiting periods may not exceed 90 days under the ACA.

keyFacts.label: Notice (employer)
keyFacts.value: None for individual terminations. WARN requires 60 days' notice for plant closings/mass layoffs at employers with 100+ employees; state mini-WARN laws are stricter (NY and NJ require 90 days).

keyFacts.label: Notice (employee)
keyFacts.value: None required by law; two weeks is customary. Employers may accept resignation effective immediately; if they do, some states then require prompt final pay.

keyFacts.label: Statutory severance
keyFacts.value: None federally. Exception: NJ WARN requires mandatory severance of one week per full year of service in covered mass layoffs (plus four weeks if notice is short). Severance is otherwise contractual or plan-based (ERISA severance plans are common).

keyFacts.label: Working hours & overtime
keyFacts.value: FLSA: time-and-a-half over 40 hours/week for non-exempt staff; no federal daily overtime or break mandate. Exempt salary level is $684/week ($35,568/yr); highly compensated employee (HCE) threshold is $107,432 (the 2024 increase was vacated Nov 2024 and DOL restored the 2019 text May 14, 2026). CA, NY, WA and CO set much higher state thresholds (verify current figures); AK, NV, CO and CA have daily overtime.

keyFacts.label: Minimum wage
keyFacts.value: Federal $7.25/hour (unchanged since 2009). Most states and many cities set higher rates, often indexed each Jan 1 (some on Jul 1). Pay the highest applicable rate at the employee's work location.

keyFacts.label: Annual leave
keyFacts.value: No federal vacation mandate. Whether accrued vacation must be paid at termination depends on state law (e.g., CA, CO, IL, MA, NE require payout or ban forfeiture); unlimited PTO policies need careful drafting in those states.

keyFacts.label: Public holidays
keyFacts.value: No private-sector holiday mandate; 11 federal holidays are the market reference (tech employers typically offer 10-12 days plus floating holidays). Holiday premium pay is not legally required.

keyFacts.label: Sick leave
keyFacts.value: No general federal paid sick leave. About 19 states plus DC and many cities mandate it (new: AK Jul 2025, NE Oct 2025; MI ESTA expanded Feb 2025; MO's voter-approved law was repealed Aug 28, 2025). IL requires paid leave for any reason; NY adds 20 hours of paid prenatal leave.

keyFacts.label: Parental leave
keyFacts.value: FMLA: 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave (50+ employees within 75 miles; 12 months and 1,250 hours of service). PWFA requires reasonable accommodation of pregnancy limitations; the PUMP Act requires lactation breaks and a private space. Paid leave comes from state PFML programs or employer policy.

keyFacts.label: Social insurance / mandatory benefits
keyFacts.value: FICA 7.65% employer + 7.65% employee (Social Security 6.2% on wages up to $184,500 in 2026; Medicare 1.45% uncapped, plus 0.9% additional employee Medicare over $200K). FUTA plus state UI, workers' comp, state disability (CA, NJ, NY, RI, HI) and state PFML. ACA employer mandate applies at 50+ FTEs.

keyFacts.label: Payroll frequency & final pay
keyFacts.value: Pay frequency is set by state law (weekly, biweekly or semimonthly depending on state and role). Final pay deadlines range from immediate (CA, CO, MA involuntary) to the next regular payday (NY, IL); there is no federal final-pay deadline.

keyFacts.label: Employee representation
keyFacts.value: No works councils. The NLRA protects non-supervisory employees' Section 7 concerted activity (e.g., discussing pay, criticizing management) whether or not a union exists. The NLRB had a 3-1 Republican majority from Aug 2026, but Stericycle, McLaren Macomb and Cemex remain binding precedent.

keyFacts.label: Data privacy law
keyFacts.value: No omnibus federal law for employee data. Sectoral rules apply: HIPAA (group health plan), FCRA (background checks), ADA/GINA/FMLA medical confidentiality, ECPA. States add IL BIPA, CA CCPA (employee data covered; see CA file), 50 breach-notification laws, SSN laws and NY/CT/DE electronic-monitoring notice laws.

keyFacts.label: Record retention
keyFacts.value: I-9: later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination. FLSA payroll: 3 years (timecards 2). Title VII/ADA personnel records: 1 year after the record or action (29 CFR 1602.14; longer once a charge is filed). FMLA: 3 years. OSHA 300 logs: 5 years; exposure/medical records: 30 years. ERISA: 6 years. Payroll tax records: 4 years.

keyFacts.label: Non-competes & IP
keyFacts.value: Governed by state law; the FTC's 2024 ban was vacated and the FTC dropped its appeals on Sept 5, 2025, but it still pursues case-by-case Section 5 enforcement. Non-competes are void in CA, ND, OK, MN (since Jul 2023) and WY (most employees, since Jul 2025), and WA's full ban starts Jun 30, 2027; income thresholds apply in CO, IL, OR, WA, VA, DC, ME and others. Invention-assignment carve-out notices are required in several states (e.g., CA, IL, MN, WA, DE, NJ, NY).

keyFacts.label: Language requirements
keyFacts.value: No federal language mandate for contracts or handbooks. Some state wage notices must be given in the employee's primary language (e.g., NY where a template exists). English-only rules need business necessity under EEOC guidelines (29 CFR 1606.7), which the EEOC's 2026 agenda lists for possible rescission.

keyFacts.label: Regulator(s)
keyFacts.value: EEOC; DOL (WHD, OSHA, EBSA, OFCCP, VETS, ETA/OFLC); NLRB; IRS/SSA; DHS (USCIS, ICE), DOS, DOJ (Civil Rights Division incl. IER; Civil Division for FCA); FTC/CFPB (FCRA, non-competes); HHS OCR (HIPAA). State labor departments, civil-rights agencies and attorneys general enforce the multi-state layer.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Federal and state workplace postings
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Post the EEOC 'Know Your Rights', FLSA, FMLA (50+), EPPA, USERRA and OSHA notices plus state/local notices. Remote workers need electronic access, and remote staff in each state must get that state's notices.

mandatoryPolicies.name: EEO, anti-harassment and complaint procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Prohibit discrimination and harassment on all protected bases (15+ employees; ADEA 20+), with multiple reporting channels and a non-retaliation promise. This is the core Faragher/Ellerth defense. Keep sexual orientation and gender identity covered (Bostock and state law) even though the EEOC rescinded its 2024 harassment guidance on Jan 22, 2026.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Title VII; ADA; ADEA; GINA; state FEP laws (NY requires a written policy)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Reasonable accommodation (disability, pregnancy, religion)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Run an interactive process for ADA and PWFA accommodation (15+ employees) and religious accommodation (undue hardship means substantial increased cost under Groff v. DeJoy, 2023). The PWFA elective-abortion provisions were vacated May 21, 2025.
mandatoryPolicies.source: ADA Title I; PWFA; 29 CFR Part 1636; Title VII

mandatoryPolicies.name: FMLA policy in handbook
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: If the employer has a handbook, it must describe FMLA rights (50+ employees). Give eligibility/rights and designation notices within 5 business days.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Lactation accommodation
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Provide reasonable break time and a private, non-bathroom space for 1 year after birth, for exempt and non-exempt staff.
mandatoryPolicies.source: FLSA Sec. 18D (PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Wage-hour, timekeeping and improper-deduction policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Require accurate time recording by non-exempt staff and prohibit off-the-clock work. Include a safe-harbor complaint process for improper salary deductions from exempt staff. Track FLSA overtime premium separately for W-2 code TT (from 2026).

mandatoryPolicies.name: State paid sick leave and PFML policies
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Adopt compliant accrual, carryover, use, notice and anti-retaliation terms for each state or city where employees work, and register for state PFML contributions (MN and DE benefits began Jan 1, 2026; ME May 1, 2026).

mandatoryPolicies.name: Pay transparency and salary history
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Include good-faith pay ranges (and benefits descriptions where required) in postings covered by CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, HI, DC, NJ, VT, MA, VA (Jul 1, 2026), ME (Jul 29, 2026), CT (Oct 1, 2026) and CA law. Do not ask about salary history where banned.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Harassment prevention training
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: NY: annual interactive training. IL: annual. CT: 2 hours within 6 months of hire (3+ employees). DE: 50+ employees, within 1 year of hire and every 2 years. ME: 15+ employees, within 1 year of hire. CA is covered in its own file.
mandatoryPolicies.source: NY Labor Law 201-g; IL Human Rights Act 2-109; CT Gen. Stat. 46a-54; DE 19 Del. C. 711A; ME 26 MRSA 807

mandatoryPolicies.name: Code of business conduct and ethics
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: A Nasdaq-listed company must adopt a code covering all directors, officers and employees, make it publicly available and disclose waivers for executives.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Nasdaq Rule 5610; SEC Item 406 of Reg S-K

mandatoryPolicies.name: Incentive-compensation clawback policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Recover erroneously awarded incentive pay from current and former executive officers after an accounting restatement, regardless of fault. Relevant to HR through executive bonus and equity plan design.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Insider trading policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Adopt and file (or explain the absence of) insider trading policies covering employees, including blackout periods and pre-clearance. Coordinate with equity administration.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Whistleblower, SOX complaint procedures and non-retaliation
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: The audit committee must have procedures for confidential, anonymous employee complaints about accounting or auditing. Agreements and policies must not impede reporting to the SEC or other agencies.
mandatoryPolicies.source: SOX Sec. 301 and 806; SEC Rule 21F-17; Dodd-Frank

mandatoryPolicies.name: Confidentiality/IP agreement with DTSA immunity notice
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Include the whistleblower immunity notice (or cross-reference a policy) in any agreement with employees, contractors or consultants governing trade secrets. Otherwise exemplary damages and attorney fees cannot be recovered against that individual. Add state invention-assignment carve-out notices.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Background check (FCRA) procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Use a standalone disclosure and written authorization, then a pre-adverse action notice (with a copy of the report and the CFPB Summary of Rights), a waiting period, and an adverse action notice. Layer state/local fair-chance rules on top (e.g., NYC, IL, WA, CA).

mandatoryPolicies.name: Form I-9 / E-Verify procedure
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Complete Form I-9 (01/20/25 edition) for every hire: Section 1 by day 1 and Section 2 within 3 business days. Do not over-document. Use E-Verify where required by state law or the FAR clause; E-Verify is also required for STEM OPT hires and for remote document review.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Group health plan compliance package
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Maintain an ERISA plan document/SPD/SMMs, HIPAA privacy and security policies for the plan, COBRA notices (20+ employees), the ACA SBC, and Medicare Part D, CHIP and WHCRA notices.
mandatoryPolicies.source: ERISA Secs. 102, 104; 45 CFR Parts 160/164; IRC 4980B; PHSA 2715

mandatoryPolicies.name: OSHA written programs
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Emergency action and fire prevention plans (must be written for more than 10 employees), a Hazard Communication program, and a Chemical Hygiene Plan for labs using hazardous chemicals. Keep injury recordkeeping unless in a partially exempt industry.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Federal contractor compliance (if applicable)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Section 503 AAP (50+ employees and $50K contract) and VEVRAA AAP (50+ employees and $200K, raised Aug 2026). File VETS-4212, list jobs with state employment services, and provide the EO 14173 certification of no illegal DEI. Drug-Free Workplace Act applies to covered contracts and grants. EO 11246 AAPs are no longer required.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Electronic monitoring notice
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Give prior written notice (and in NY get an acknowledgment) of email, phone and internet monitoring, and post a notice.
mandatoryPolicies.source: NY Civil Rights Law 52-c; CT Gen. Stat. 31-48d; DE 19 Del. C. 705

mandatoryPolicies.name: AI in employment decisions
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: NYC: annual independent bias audit, published summary and 10-business-day candidate notice for automated employment decision tools. IL: notice of AI use and no discriminatory AI or zip-code proxies (from Jan 1, 2026). CO SB 26-189 notice and adverse-decision explanation duties start Jan 1, 2027.
mandatoryPolicies.source: NYC Local Law 144 of 2021; 775 ILCS 5/2-102(L) (HB 3773); Colorado SB 26-189

mandatoryPolicies.name: Biometric privacy policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: If fingerprint or face data is used (timeclocks, lab or cleanroom access), publish a retention and destruction schedule and get written informed consent before collection (IL). The 2024 amendment limits recovery to one violation per person.
mandatoryPolicies.source: 740 ILCS 14 (BIPA) as amended by SB 2979 (2024); Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 503.001; RCW 19.375

mandatoryPolicies.name: Drug, alcohol and cannabis policy
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Define testing triggers and consequences, and carve out state-protected off-duty cannabis use (e.g., NY, NJ, CA, MN, WA pre-hire) except for safety-sensitive or federally regulated roles.
mandatoryPolicies.source: State cannabis and testing laws; ADA (current illegal drug users not protected)

hiring.detail: Ranges are required in postings covered by CO (2021, all employers), WA (15+), NY (4+), HI (50+), DC, MD (Oct 2024), IL (15+, Jan 2025), MN (30+, Jan 2025), NJ (10+, Jun 2025), VT (5+, Jul 2025), MA (25+, Oct 29, 2025), Cleveland (15+, Oct 2025), VA (all, Jul 1, 2026), ME (10+, Jul 29, 2026), CT (all, Oct 1, 2026) and DE (26+, Sept 26, 2027). Many reach remote roles, so the practical rule is a good-faith range plus a benefits summary on every US posting.

About 20+ states and cities bar asking about or relying on pay history (e.g., NY, NJ, MA, IL, CO, WA, OR, DE, VA from Jul 2026). Train recruiters to ask about pay expectations instead, and remove the question from ATS forms.

hiring.req: Background checks under FCRA plus fair-chance laws
hiring.detail: Use a standalone disclosure and authorization, a pre-adverse action notice with the report and Summary of Rights, a waiting period (commonly 5 business days), then an adverse action notice. Delay criminal history questions until after a conditional offer where required (NYC, IL, WA, CA and others) and do an individualized assessment.
hiring.cite: 15 U.S.C. 1681b(b), 1681m; NYC Fair Chance Act; 775 ILCS 5/2-103.1

hiring.req: AI and automated tools in screening
hiring.detail: NYC LL 144: annual independent bias audit, public summary, and notice 10 business days before use. IL HB 3773 (from Jan 1, 2026): notice of AI use and no discriminatory effect; IDHR postponed its notice rules Jun 2, 2026 but the statute applies. Colorado replaced its AI Act with SB 26-189 (signed May 14, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027; notice and explanation model). Title VII disparate impact still applies despite EO 14281.
hiring.cite: NYC LL 144; 775 ILCS 5/2-102(L); CO SB 26-189; Title VII 703(k)

hiring.detail: No race- or sex-restricted slates, internships, fellowships or hiring targets, and no pay tied to demographic goals. Ames v. Ohio (Jun 5, 2025) removed extra hurdles for majority-group plaintiffs. DOJ's first DEI False Claims Act settlement (IBM, $17M, Apr 10, 2026) targeted diverse-slate rules and demographic-linked bonuses. Keep outreach broad and open to all.
hiring.cite: Title VII; 42 U.S.C. 1981; EO 14173; EEOC/DOJ technical assistance (Mar 19, 2025)

hiring.detail: No disability inquiries or medical exams before a conditional offer; post-offer exams must apply to all entrants in the job category. Never ask about family medical history (GINA). Check state limits on pre-employment cannabis testing (e.g., NY, NJ, MN, WA).
hiring.cite: ADA 42 U.S.C. 12112(d); GINA Title II; state law

hiring.detail: H-1B cap registration is in March and uses wage-weighted selection (effective Feb 27, 2026; Level IV gets 4 entries, Level I gets 1); FY2027 had 211,600 registrations and no second lottery. The $100K fee for beneficiaries abroad was vacated nationwide (D. Mass., Jun 8, 2026; 1st Cir. denied stay Jul 24) but was extended by proclamation to Sept 21, 2027. A proposed $103,265 fee on cap petitions (NPRM Aug 25, 2026) could hit FY2028 filings. Consider O-1, L-1, TN, E-3 and H-1B1 alternatives, and plan PERM early (DOL's Mar 31, 2026 NPRM would raise Level I-IV prevailing wages to the 34th/52nd/70th/88th percentiles).
hiring.cite: INA 214(g); 8 CFR 214.2(h)(8)(iii); Proclamation 10973 and Sept 18, 2026 extension; 20 CFR 655/656

hiring.detail: STEM OPT (24 months) requires E-Verify, a Form I-983 training plan and reporting. DHS's duration-of-status final rule (effective Sept 15, 2026) gives F-1s fixed I-94 end dates, so OPT hires may need both I-539 and I-765 approvals before starting. Build start-date buffers. Cap-gap extends status to Apr 1 for H-1B change-of-status filers.
hiring.cite: 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)-(12); DHS F-1 fixed admission final rule (Jul 17, 2026)

hiring.detail: Offer letters should include at-will language and exempt status. Condition the offer on signing a confidentiality/invention assignment agreement with the DTSA notice and state carve-outs. Do not use non-competes for employees in MN, ND, OK, WY, CA or (from Jun 30, 2027) WA, and check income thresholds (CO, IL, OR, VA, DC, ME, MA garden leave). FL's CHOICE Act (Jul 2025) instead favors enforcement.

hiring.req: Export-control screening kept separate from I-9
hiring.detail: For roles with access to EAR/ITAR-controlled technology, ask all finalists a narrow, uniform export-control question after the offer stage where possible. Do not use the I-9 or document requests for this; citizenship discrimination and document abuse are barred. Form I-129 Part 6 requires a deemed-export attestation (covered in the export-control file).
hiring.cite: 8 U.S.C. 1324b; DOJ/BIS/DDTC joint fact sheet on export controls and hiring (2023)

onboarding.detail: Use the 01/20/25 edition (expires 05/31/2027); the 08/01/23 print with a 07/31/2026 expiration may not be used for new hires. E-Verify employers in good standing may examine documents remotely by live video (keep copies and check the alternative-procedure box). ICE guidance of Mar 16, 2026 reclassified 10+ error types (e.g., missing Section 2 document data or start date) as substantive, uncurable violations ($288-$2,861 per form), so audit before any Notice of Inspection.

Required under the FAR E-Verify clause for federal contracts and by state law in several states (e.g., AZ, AL, MS, SC, GA, NC 25+, FL 25+, UT 150+; verify thresholds), and for STEM OPT employers. Create cases by day 3 and follow Tentative Nonconfirmation procedures exactly.

onboarding.req: Tax, new-hire reporting and state registration for remote staff
onboarding.detail: Collect Form W-4 and state withholding forms. Report new hires to the state within 20 days (some states are shorter). Before the first payroll, register for withholding, UI, PFML and local taxes in each remote employee's work state or city.

onboarding.req: Wage notices and state onboarding packets
onboarding.detail: Provide state hire notices, e.g., NY Wage Theft Prevention Act notice (pay rate, payday, exempt status, in the primary language), NJ/NY/CT/WA/MN paid leave notices, state PFML notices, and workers' comp and UI pamphlets.
onboarding.cite: NY Labor Law 195(1); state PFML/sick leave laws

onboarding.detail: Get acknowledgment of the handbook with state addenda. Under Stericycle (still binding), confidentiality, social media, recording, civility and media-contact rules must be narrowly tailored and include a Section 7 savings clause. GC 26-04 (Aug 26, 2026) signals change, but only a Board decision changes the standard.
NY: at hire and annually, interactive. IL: annually. CT: 2 hours within 6 months (3+ employees). DE: within 1 year (50+ employees). ME: within 1 year (15+ employees). Keep completion records.

Waiting period of no more than 90 days (ACA). Give the COBRA general notice within 90 days of coverage, plus SBC and HIPAA special enrollment rights (30 days). Auto-enroll new 401(k) plans (SECURE 2.0 mandatory auto-enrollment for plans established after Dec 29, 2022).
In NY, CT and DE, give written notice of monitoring at hire and get acknowledgment (NY). Disclose AI productivity or keystroke tools.
onboarding.cite: NY Civ. Rights Law 52-c; CT 31-48d; DE 19 Del. C. 705

onboarding.detail: Sign before the start date or on day 1, with the DTSA immunity notice, SEC Rule 21F-17 carve-out, NLRA savings clause and state invention-assignment notices. Collect a prior-inventions schedule and a written affirmation that no prior employer's confidential information is being brought in.
onboarding.cite: 18 U.S.C. 1833(b); SEC Rule 21F-17; state invention statutes

payAndPayroll.detail: Standard salary level is $684/week and HCE is $107,432 (the 2024 rule was vacated in Texas v. DOL on Nov 15, 2024; DOL restored the 2019 text May 14, 2026). The computer-employee hourly alternative is $27.63/hr. E.M.D. Sales v. Carrera (Jan 2025) set a preponderance standard for proving exemptions. Apply higher state thresholds (CA, NY, WA, CO) and state duties tests.

payAndPayroll.req: Regular rate and overtime for non-exempt technicians
payAndPayroll.detail: Include non-discretionary bonuses, shift differentials and some awards in the regular rate. Pay for on-call time that is engaged to wait. Apply daily overtime in CA, AK, NV and CO.

payAndPayroll.req: OBBBA qualified overtime and tips reporting
payAndPayroll.detail: Employees may deduct the FLSA-required overtime premium (not state-only or contractual overtime) up to $12,500 ($25,000 joint), phasing out above $150K MAGI, for 2025-2028. Employers must report qualified overtime on 2026 Forms W-2 (Box 12 code TT; tips code TP; Box 14b occupation code). IRS gave transition relief for 2025. Payroll systems must isolate the premium portion.

payAndPayroll.req: Minimum wage and pay frequency by work location
payAndPayroll.detail: Federal minimum is $7.25; apply state and city minimums (many indexed Jan 1). Pay frequency is state-specific (e.g., NY manual workers weekly; MA non-exempt weekly or biweekly). Remote staff follow their work state's rules.

The federal EPA covers equal work regardless of employer size; state laws (NY, MA, IL, CO, WA, NJ, MD, OR) use 'substantially similar' or broader comparators. IL requires an Equal Pay Registration Certificate (100+ IL employees, every 2 years). MA requires an annual workforce demographic report by Feb 1 (100+ MA employees). Run privileged pay-equity audits.

Social Security wage base is $184,500; 0.9% Additional Medicare withholding applies over $200K. Supplemental withholding is 22%, or a mandatory 37% on supplemental wages over $1M (relevant to RSU vesting). Watch multi-state sourcing of equity income for mobile employees.

The Form 1099-NEC/MISC threshold rises to $2,000 for payments after Dec 31, 2025 (indexed later). DOL proposed (Feb 26, 2026) to replace the 2024 independent contractor rule with the 2021 core-factor test (control and profit/loss opportunity); a final rule is pending. State ABC tests (MA, NJ, IL for some purposes) are stricter.

From Jul 4, 2026, employers may contribute up to $2,500/yr per employee tax-free to the Trump accounts of employees or their dependents under a separate written IRC 128 plan that meets nondiscrimination rules. Report with W-2 code TA. Proposed regs were issued Aug 11, 2026 (comments due Sept 25; hearing Oct 15). DOL TR 2026-02 says these generally are not ERISA plans if conditions are met.
payAndPayroll.cite: IRC 128, 530A (OBBBA); Prop. Treas. Reg. (Aug 2026); DOL TR 2026-02

payAndPayroll.detail: Many states require written, voluntary authorization for deductions and restrict self-help recovery of overpayments, equipment costs or training repayment (e.g., NY 193, IL, WA). Deductions from exempt salaries must follow 29 CFR 541.602.

Put sales commission plans in writing, signed where required (e.g., NY Labor Law 191(1)(c); MN; CA separate), and spell out earning, draws and post-termination payment. Unclear plans risk treble damages under state wage laws.

timeAndLeave.detail: Up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave (26 weeks for military caregivers) with continued group health coverage, for 50+ employees within 75 miles and 12 months/1,250 hours of service. Remote employees count at the worksite they report to. Give notices within 5 business days and track intermittent leave.

Accommodate known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth or related conditions (15+ employees), including leave, telework and temporary suspension of essential functions. Do not require medical documentation when the need is obvious. Elective-abortion provisions were vacated (W.D. La., May 21, 2025); the EEOC's 2026 agenda plans an NPRM narrowing 'related medical conditions'.

timeAndLeave.req: State paid family and medical leave (multi-state)
timeAndLeave.detail: Programs run in CA, NJ, NY, RI, WA, MA, CT, OR, CO and DC; MN and DE paid benefits from Jan 1, 2026; ME benefits from May 1, 2026; MD contributions start Jan 1, 2027 with benefits from Jan 3, 2028. CO FAMLI added 12 weeks of NICU leave and cut the premium to 0.88% in 2026. WA extended job protection to 25+ employers in 2026. Register, withhold, post notices, and coordinate with FMLA and STD.

timeAndLeave.req: State and local paid sick leave (multi-state)
timeAndLeave.detail: About 19 states plus DC (e.g., AZ, CO, CT, IL any reason, MA, MD, ME, MI ESTA, MN, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA, AK Jul 2025, NE Oct 2025) and many cities (NYC, Chicago, Philadelphia, Seattle). MO repealed its law effective Aug 28, 2025. NY adds 20 hours of paid prenatal leave. A single generous PTO policy can satisfy most laws if it meets the strictest accrual, carryover, use and notice rules.
timeAndLeave.cite: State/local sick leave laws; NY Labor Law 196-b

timeAndLeave.detail: Leave beyond FMLA or policy limits can be a reasonable accommodation. Avoid rigid maximum-leave or '100% healed' rules and document the interactive process.
Reemployment rights for up to 5 cumulative years of service, with seniority/escalator protection and 401(k) make-up contributions. Health coverage continuation is available for up to 24 months.

No federal rule. Accrued vacation is treated as wages (no forfeiture, or payout at separation) in states such as CA, CO, IL, MA, MT and NE. Unlimited PTO still needs clear written terms to avoid accrual arguments.

Jury and witness duty, voting, crime-victim, bereavement (e.g., IL FBLA, CA), organ/bone-marrow donation, blood donation (NY), school activities and domestic-violence leave vary by state. Include these in state handbook addenda.

timeAndLeave.req: Hours recording for remote non-exempt staff
timeAndLeave.detail: Require daily time entry, pay for all hours worked including pre-shift log-in and short breaks under 20 minutes, and apply state meal and rest rules (e.g., WA, OR, CO, NY, IL for some workers).

benefits.req: Mandatory Roth catch-up for high earners (from 2026)
benefits.detail: Participants with prior-year FICA wages (W-2 Box 3, same employer) over $150,000 (2025 wages) must make catch-ups as Roth. Plans without a Roth feature cannot offer them catch-ups. Final regs (Sept 16, 2025) permit deemed Roth elections, generally apply from 2027, and allow good-faith compliance in 2026.

HSA $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family (+$1,000 at 55+). HDHP minimum deductible $1,700/$3,400 and out-of-pocket maximum $8,500/$17,000. Health FSA $3,400 (carryover $680). Dependent care FSA $7,500 per household (OBBBA, from 2026, not indexed). Transit/parking $340/month. Adoption assistance $17,670.
benefits.cite: IRS 2026 HSA/HDHP and COLA announcements; IRC 129 as amended by OBBBA

benefits.detail: IRC 127 student-loan repayment made permanent, with the $5,250 cap indexed after 2026. HSA telehealth pre-deductible safe harbor made permanent. Direct primary care fees (up to $150/month self-only) and bronze/catastrophic exchange plans are HSA-compatible from 2026. The 45F childcare and 45S paid-leave credits were expanded and 45S made permanent. The bicycle-commuting and moving-expense exclusions were permanently eliminated.

At 50+ FTEs, offer affordable, minimum-value coverage to at least 95% of full-time employees (30+ hours/week). 2026 affordability is 9.96% of household income (FPL safe harbor about $129.89/month self-only; verify). 2026 penalties: 4980H(a) $3,340 and 4980H(b) $5,010 per year. Furnish Forms 1095-C by about Mar 2 and e-file 1094-C/1095-C by Mar 31. The 2024 reporting relief laws allow on-request furnishing to non-full-time individuals, set a 6-year limitations period, and give 90 days to answer Letter 226-J.
benefits.cite: IRC 4980H, 6055, 6056; Paperwork Burden Reduction Act and Employer Reporting Improvement Act (2024)

benefits.detail: Maintain a written plan document and SPD (SMM within 210 days after plan year end), a fiduciary committee charter and minutes, fee benchmarking and 404a-5 disclosures. File Form 5500 by the last day of the 7th month (Jul 31 for calendar plans; Form 5558 extends to Oct 15).
Applies at 20+ employees: election notice within 44 days if the employer is administrator, 60-day election, 18/29/36 months. State mini-COBRA laws cover small insured plans (e.g., NY 36 months).

benefits.req: HIPAA privacy and security for the group health plan
benefits.detail: Plan sponsors that see PHI need firewall amendments, policies, training and business associate agreements. The 2024 reproductive-health privacy rule was vacated nationally (Purl v. HHS, N.D. Tex., June 2025); earlier rules remain.

Keep NQTL comparative analyses. Enforcement of the new provisions of the 2024 MHPAEA final rule was paused in May 2025, but the 2021 CAA analysis duty remains. File RxDC reports by Jun 1 and pay the PCORI fee by Jul 31 (self-insured plans).

Send the Medicare Part D creditable coverage notice by Oct 15, plus CHIP, WHCRA, the HIPAA privacy notice (every 3 years), SBC and wellness program notices. Recheck ACA affordability against next year's percentage when setting contributions.

performanceAndConduct.detail: Do not discipline employees for discussing pay or conditions, for group complaints, or for protected social media posts, and scrub policies banning 'negative' comments. Stericycle (2023) and the Amazon captive-audience decision (Nov 2024) remain binding while the new Republican majority (Macy confirmed Aug 7, 2026; GC Crystal Carey) looks for vehicles to overrule them.

Investigate promptly with a trained, impartial investigator, document findings and prevent retaliation. The EEOC rescinded its 2024 harassment guidance (Jan 22, 2026, vote 2-1), but Title VII, Bostock and state laws covering sexual orientation and gender identity are unchanged.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Title VII; Bostock v. Clayton County (2020)

performanceAndConduct.detail: Muldrow v. St. Louis (2024) lets transfer or assignment claims proceed on 'some harm', so document legitimate reasons for job changes as well as terminations. Keep calibration consistent across demographic groups and check performance-improvement-plan outcomes for adverse impact.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Muldrow v. City of St. Louis, 601 U.S. 346 (2024)

performanceAndConduct.detail: ERGs, mentoring, sponsorship and leadership programs must be open to all. Remove demographic-linked bonus metrics and diverse-slate mandates. Federal contractors and grantees certify under EO 14173, and a Mar 26, 2026 EO adds contractor certification, subcontractor monitoring and FCA materiality clauses. Keep legal review under privilege.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Title VII; 42 U.S.C. 1981; EO 14173; EO of Mar 26, 2026; DOJ Civil Rights Fraud Initiative

performanceAndConduct.req: National-origin and citizenship fairness in a visa-heavy workforce
performanceAndConduct.detail: The EEOC, DOJ IER and DOL (Project Firewall, launched Sept 19, 2025) are targeting preferences for visa workers over US workers as well as citizenship discrimination against work-authorized non-citizens. Document neutral, job-related selection criteria for both.

No policy or agreement may impede reporting to the SEC, EEOC, NLRB or OSHA. Route SOX-related complaints to the audit committee and train managers on anti-retaliation (SOX 806; OSHA 11(c); Dodd-Frank).

Several states ban mandatory meetings on political or religious matters, including unionization (e.g., CT, NY, MN, IL, ME, OR, WA, VT, NJ, CA). Some bans face NLRA preemption challenges, so check status by state.
Several states protect lawful off-duty conduct or cannabis use (e.g., NY Labor Law 201-d, NJ CREAMMA, CO, IL). Discipline for impairment at work, not for off-duty use, unless an exception applies.

performanceAndConduct.req: AI and monitoring in performance management
performanceAndConduct.detail: Automated performance or scheduling tools can trigger IL HB 3773 notice duties (from Jan 2026), CO SB 26-189 duties (from Jan 2027) and NY/CT/DE monitoring notices. Keep a human review step for adverse decisions.

termination.req: At-will with a legitimate, documented reason
termination.detail: Decisions that are at-will in law are still judged for pretext. Check consistency with past cases, timing near protected activity (complaints, leave, accommodation requests) and statements by decision-makers. The EEOC charge window is 180 or 300 days.

With 100+ employees, give 60 days' notice of a plant closing (50+ job losses at a single site) or a mass layoff (500+, or 50-499 if at least 33% of the site). Remote employees are attributed to the site they report to. Penalty is up to 60 days' back pay and benefits.

NY: 50+ employees, 90 days' notice, triggered at 25+ losses; the NY DOL form asks whether AI or automation drove the cuts. NJ: 100+ employees anywhere, 90 days' notice when 50+ are laid off at or reporting to NJ sites, plus mandatory severance of 1 week per year of service. IL: 75+ employees, 60 days. Also check WA (Jul 27, 2025: 50+ employees, 60 days), CA (separate file), TN, IA, WI, ME and others.
termination.cite: NY Labor Law 860; N.J.S.A. 34:21-1 et seq.; 820 ILCS 65

termination.detail: Individual: 21 days to consider and 7 days to revoke. Group program: 45 days, 7 to revoke, plus a written disclosure of the decisional unit, eligibility factors, and job titles and ages of those selected and not selected. The release must be written in plain language, reference the ADEA, advise consulting an attorney and give consideration beyond what is already owed.

Run a privileged statistical review by age, sex, race and national origin of selections within each decisional unit, and document objective criteria. Check the effect on visa holders and on employees on leave or with pending complaints.

termination.req: Terminating H-1B and other sponsored workers
termination.detail: Notify USCIS, withdraw the LCA and offer return transportation to effect a bona fide termination; otherwise back-wage liability continues. Workers have a 60-day grace period. Under the Sept 18, 2026 EO, agencies weigh the employer's layoffs in the past year and planned layoffs when adjudicating LCAs and petitions, so coordinate RIF timing with pending H-1B filings.

Examples: CA immediate (see CA file); CO immediate on involuntary termination; MA same day on involuntary termination; CT next business day on discharge; TX within 6 days on discharge; NY, IL and many others next regular payday; WA end of pay period. Include accrued vacation where state law treats it as wages. Waiting-time and penalty wages apply in several states.

Many states require written separation or UI-information notices (e.g., NY Record of Employment IA 12.3, NJ BC-10, IL, PA, MD, CO). Also required: COBRA qualifying-event notice to the administrator within 30 days, and a HIPAA special-enrollment reminder.

termination.req: Severance agreement terms (NLRA, Speak Out Act, SEC)
termination.detail: McLaren Macomb (2023) still bars offering non-supervisory employees severance with broad confidentiality or non-disparagement clauses. Carve out Section 7 rights and agency reporting, and limit confidentiality to agreement terms and trade secrets. Pre-dispute NDAs cannot bar disclosure of sexual assault or harassment (Speak Out Act). State laws (NY, NJ, IL, WA) restrict confidentiality about discrimination facts.
termination.cite: McLaren Macomb, 372 NLRB No. 58 (2023); 42 U.S.C. 19401-19404; SEC Rule 21F-17

exit.req: Return of property and trade-secret protection
exit.detail: Get equipment back, cut access on the last day (or at notice for high-risk departures), review download activity for 30-90 days before exit and forensically image devices of key engineers. Get a signed certification of return and deletion and remind the employee of confidentiality duties.
exit.cite: DTSA 18 U.S.C. 1836; state trade secret acts

exit.detail: Rely on NDAs and targeted customer and employee non-solicits. Do not threaten to enforce non-competes that are void (MN, ND, OK, WY, CA; WA from Jun 30, 2027, when employers must also send notices to affected current and former workers by Oct 1, 2027 that their non-competes are void). The FTC may still challenge overbroad non-competes case by case (e.g., Gateway Services, Sept 2025).
exit.cite: State non-compete laws; FTC Act Sec. 5

exit.detail: Pay by the state deadline (see termination). Pay earned commissions under the written plan terms. Some states require payment of accrued vacation. Follow the plan terms on equity: vesting stops at termination and the post-termination exercise window is usually 90 days for ISOs.

Send the COBRA election notice (44 days if the employer is administrator), 401(k) distribution and rollover notices, and FSA run-out and HSA portability information. Offer life and disability conversion or portability.
Adopt a neutral reference policy (dates and title). Some states require a service letter on request stating the reason for separation (e.g., MN within 10 working days of request, MO, KS, NV; verify).

H-1B: withdraw the LCA, notify USCIS, offer return fare. STEM OPT: notify the DSO within 5 business days and submit the final I-983 evaluation. Retain I-9s for the required period and E-Verify records as required.

Revoke access to controlled technology repositories and document the date. For foreign-national departures, update deemed-export license records and technology control plans (coordinate with the export-control team).
Ask departing employees about unreported compliance concerns and route any to the audit committee or legal. Do not condition severance on waiving SEC award rights.

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: I-9: 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, whichever is later. FLSA payroll 3 years and timecards 2 years. Personnel/EEO records 1 year (keep through final disposition once a charge is filed). ADEA payroll 3 years. FMLA 3 years. OSHA 300/300A/301: 5 years. Exposure/medical records: employment plus 30 years. ERISA 6 years. Tax 4 years. FCRA reports: 5 years is a litigation-safe practice. Apply litigation holds as needed.

Keep medical, genetic, accommodation and FMLA records in confidential files separate from personnel files, and keep I-9s in a separate binder or system to limit audit exposure and discrimination inferences.

The 2025 EEO-1 collection had not opened as of Sept 2026. The EEOC voted in July 2026 to propose rescinding EEO-1 through EEO-6 reporting (comments closed Aug 24, 2026); existing requirements stand until a final rule. Keep voluntary self-ID data separate from decision-makers. State reports continue (IL certificate, MA demographic report, CA pay data).

IL: a public retention and destruction policy, informed written consent (an electronic signature is allowed since 2024) and no sale of data. Damages are $1,000 negligent and $5,000 reckless per person after the 2024 amendment. TX and WA have similar laws and CO added biometric rules in 2025. Common triggers are timeclocks, lab access and ID verification tools.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: 740 ILCS 14; Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 503.001; RCW 19.375

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Get FCRA authorization for any consumer report, including third-party social media screening. Dispose of reports securely (FACTA Disposal Rule). Comply with state rules on credit checks (e.g., NYC, IL, WA, CO bans for most roles).

All 50 states require breach notification, some with regulator notice or deadlines (e.g., 30-45 days). Limit SSN display, encrypt HRIS exports and set vendor security terms. Public-company cyber incident disclosure (Form 8-K Item 1.05) can be triggered by an HR data breach.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: State breach laws; SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Many states give employees rights to inspect or copy their personnel files within set deadlines (e.g., IL, MN, WA, OR, MA, MI, CT). Build a single request process.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: 820 ILCS 40; Minn. Stat. 181.961; M.G.L. c.149 s.52C

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: The CA CCPA covers employee data (see the CA file). Other state comprehensive privacy laws generally exempt employment data, but NY, CT and DE monitoring notices, BIPA, AI notices (NYC, IL, CO) and genetic-privacy laws still apply.

recordsAndPrivacy.req: Global data transfers from the US HRIS
recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Transfers of non-US employee data into the US HRIS need EU/UK/Swiss mechanisms (Data Privacy Framework certification or SCCs). DOJ's bulk sensitive data rule (effective Apr 2025) restricts giving covered foreign persons (e.g., China-linked vendors) access to bulk US employee data.

healthSafety.detail: Keep the workplace free of recognized serious hazards. Office and lab sites need walking-working surfaces, electrical safety (1910 Subpart S; NFPA 70E for test benches), lockout/tagout for equipment servicing, PPE hazard assessments and exit routes.

Record work-related injuries within 7 days (employers with more than 10 employees, unless the NAICS is partially exempt). Post the certified 300A from Feb 1 to Apr 30 and keep records 5 years. Report fatalities within 8 hours and inpatient hospitalizations, amputations or eye loss within 24 hours.

Submit 300A data by Mar 2 (Mar 2, 2026 for 2025 data) for establishments with 250+ employees, or 20-249 in designated industries. Establishments with 100+ employees in Appendix B industries also submit 300/301 case data. Check each site's NAICS code.

Characterization, failure-analysis and reliability labs that use hazardous chemicals at laboratory scale need a written Chemical Hygiene Plan, a Chemical Hygiene Officer, exposure monitoring and medical consultation. HazCom 2024 (GHS Rev. 7 alignment) phases in labels, SDSs and training updates in 2026-27 (verify current compliance dates).
Plans must be written if there are more than 10 employees. Cover evacuation, gas and chemical alarms and accounting for employees, and hold regular drills.

Follow ANSI Z136 and a laser safety officer program for photonics and test lasers. Register X-ray and inspection equipment with the state radiation program. OSHA enforces these through the General Duty Clause and the PPE standards.
healthSafety.cite: OSHA General Duty Clause; 29 CFR 1910.132; state radiation rules

healthSafety.detail: Employees may report injuries and hazards without retaliation. Drug-testing and incentive programs must not deter reporting.

healthSafety.req: Heat, workplace violence and state plans
healthSafety.detail: A federal heat-illness rule is still proposed (verify status); CA, WA, OR, MD and NV have heat rules. There is no federal workplace-violence standard, though some states have one (see the CA file for SB 553). Some states run OSHA-approved state plans with stricter rules (e.g., WA, OR, MI, MN, NC).

OSHA does not inspect home offices, but injuries in the course of work are recordable and compensable. Buy workers' comp coverage in each remote employee's state (monopolistic state funds in ND, OH, WA, WY) and give ergonomic guidance.
healthSafety.cite: OSHA CPL 2-0.125 (home-based worksites); state WC laws

terminationDeepDive.voluntary: No statutory notice either way; two weeks is customary and senior engineers often give 2-4 weeks. An employer may accept a resignation early, which may start the final-pay clock and, in some states (e.g., NY, IL), affects UI eligibility. Garden leave is not statutory, except that MA's Noncompetition Agreement Act requires garden leave (50% of base) or other agreed consideration to enforce a non-compete. Buyouts of notice are uncommon. Pay out accrued PTO where state law or policy requires it, and run the IP and trade-secret exit protocol for departures to competitors.
terminationDeepDive.involuntary: At-will allows termination without cause or notice, but the reason must not be discriminatory or retaliatory (protected characteristics; complaints; FMLA, PWFA or ADA requests; whistleblowing; Section 7 activity; workers' comp claims). Best practice: document performance issues and warnings, have HR and legal review against comparators, check for recent protected activity, give a truthful, consistent reason, and hold a short, respectful meeting with a witness. Montana requires good cause after probation. Written-contract executives need for-cause definitions and cure periods honored. Discrimination claims carry uncapped back and front pay; compensatory and punitive damages are capped at $50K-$300K by size under Title VII/ADA (42 U.S.C. 1981a) but uncapped under Section 1981 race claims and many state laws.
terminationDeepDive.redundancy: No 'redundancy' concept; RIFs are at-will but must be non-discriminatory. Federal WARN: 100+ employees; 60 days' notice to employees, the state dislocated-worker unit and local government for plant closings (50+ at a site) or mass layoffs (500+, or 50-499 and at least 33%), aggregated over 90 days. State mini-WARN laws are stricter: NY (50+ employees, 90 days, 25+ losses), NJ (90 days, mandatory severance 1 week per year of service), IL (75+ employees, 60 days), plus CA and others. Group releases for 40+ employees need OWBPA disclosures and 45/7 days. Run adverse-impact analysis, check H-1B implications (the Sept 18, 2026 EO makes layoffs a factor in H-1B and LCA adjudication), and check federal contractor and state separation-notice duties. No government consultation or approval is required beyond WARN notices.
terminationDeepDive.finalPayTiming: There is no federal deadline beyond the next regular payday for FLSA minimum wage and overtime; state law controls. Examples: CA immediate on discharge, 72 hours on resignation without notice (see CA file, with waiting-time penalties up to 30 days' wages); CO immediate on involuntary termination (penalty is the greater of 2x the unpaid amount or $1,000, more if willful, plus fees); MA same day on involuntary termination and next payday on resignation (mandatory treble damages); CT next business day on discharge; TX within 6 calendar days on discharge; MN within 24 hours of demand; NY, IL, NJ, PA next regular payday; WA end of pay period. Pay accrued vacation where required (e.g., CA, CO, IL, MA, NE).
requiredDocuments: Final paycheck and wage statement by the state deadline
COBRA election notice (via administrator; 44 days if employer-administered) and HIPAA/state continuation notices
State separation or UI notice where required (e.g., NY IA 12.3, NJ BC-10, IL, PA, MD, CO)
OWBPA disclosure exhibit (group programs, age 40+) and release with 21/45-day review and 7-day revocation
WARN / state mini-WARN notices to employees, state agencies and local officials when triggered
401(k) distribution and rollover (402(f)) notice; FSA/HSA and life insurance conversion information
Equity award termination statement (vesting stop, exercise window)
Service letter on request in states that require it (e.g., MN, MO)
H-1B: LCA withdrawal, USCIS notification and written offer of return transportation
Return-of-property and confidentiality acknowledgment (not legally mandated but standard)
terminationDeepDive.releaseAgreements: General releases of federal and state claims are enforceable if knowing and voluntary and supported by new consideration. For employees 40+, OWBPA requires plain language, express reference to the ADEA, advice to consult an attorney, 21 days (45 for group programs) to consider and 7 days to revoke, plus decisional-unit disclosures for groups. FLSA wage claims generally need DOL or court approval to release (circuit split). Non-releasable: EEOC charge filing (the right to monetary recovery can be waived), NLRB charges, SEC whistleblower awards, unemployment and workers' comp benefits, and vested ERISA benefits. McLaren Macomb (still binding in Sept 2026) makes broad confidentiality and non-disparagement clauses unlawful for non-supervisory employees, so include a Section 7 and agency-reporting carve-out. The Speak Out Act voids pre-dispute NDAs for sexual assault and harassment disputes. State add-ons: NY requires a 21-day consideration and 7-day revocation plus complainant preference before confidentiality of discrimination facts; NJ bars confidentiality of discrimination facts; IL requires specific terms for confidentiality of unlawful-practice facts; WA (Silenced No More Act) bars NDAs covering illegal discrimination or harassment; CA is covered separately.
terminationDeepDive.typicalPackage: Market practice (not legal requirement) for US tech and semiconductor RIFs, 2025-26: 8-16 weeks' base pay as a floor for individual contributors, often structured as 2 weeks per year of service plus a base amount (e.g., 4-8 weeks) with a cap (often 26 weeks). Directors and VPs get 3-6 months, and executives follow severance or change-in-control plans (commonly 6-12 months' base plus pro-rata bonus; 12-24 months in change-in-control situations). Also common: a COBRA premium subsidy for the severance period, outplacement for 1-3 months, and pro-rated or accelerated vesting of RSUs that would vest within 1-3 months (less common for broad RIFs). WARN pay-in-lieu is often folded into the package. Release consideration must be in addition to anything already owed.

recentChanges.title: H-1B $100K proclamation extended to Sept 2027; layoffs EO issued, but fee remains vacated
recentChanges.detail: On Sept 18, 2026 the President extended Proclamation 10973's $100,000 payment for H-1B petitions for beneficiaries abroad or requesting consular notification through Sept 21, 2027. A separate EO directs DOL, DHS and DOS to weigh an employer's past-year and planned layoffs when adjudicating LCAs, petitions and visas, and has DOL review prior LCAs within 30 days. The fee itself was vacated nationwide by D. Mass. (Jun 8, 2026), and the 1st Circuit denied a stay (Jul 24, 2026). A separate challenge is on appeal in the D.C. Circuit after a district court upheld the fee.

recentChanges.title: F-1 'duration of status' replaced by fixed admission periods
recentChanges.detail: DHS final rule (published Jul 17, effective Sept 15, 2026) gives F-1 students fixed I-94 end dates. OPT and STEM OPT continue, but many students will need an I-539 extension of stay alongside the I-765, which can delay start dates. Transition relief runs to Mar 18, 2027.

recentChanges.title: DHS proposes $103,265 fee on every cap-subject H-1B petition
recentChanges.detail: NPRM published Aug 25, 2026 (comments due Sept 24, 2026). The fee would apply to all cap-subject petitions, including master's cap cases, filed from the FY2028 season (Apr 1, 2027). Cap-exempt petitions, extensions, amendments and changes of employer are excluded.

recentChanges.title: OFCCP final rules: EO 11246 regulations rescinded; Section 503 and VEVRAA narrowed
recentChanges.detail: Published Aug 21, 2026. EO 11246 affirmative action regulations are removed. For Section 503 (effective Sept 21, 2026), the CC-305 self-ID form, the 7% utilization goal and disability data collection are eliminated and the coverage threshold rises to $20K. The VEVRAA AAP threshold rises to $200K, while veteran AAPs, benchmarks, job listing and VETS-4212 (due Sept 30) remain.

recentChanges.title: NLRB gains a Republican majority; GC targets McLaren Macomb and Stericycle
recentChanges.detail: James Macy (R) and David Prouty (D) were confirmed Aug 7, 2026, giving a 3-1 Board (Chair Murphy, Mayer, Macy, Prouty). GC Crystal Carey's GC 26-04 (Aug 26, 2026) lists 12 areas of Biden-era precedent to challenge. Stericycle, McLaren Macomb and Cemex remain binding until overruled.

recentChanges.title: Trump account employer contributions: proposed regulations
recentChanges.detail: Treasury and IRS proposed rules (Aug 11, 2026) for IRC 128 employer contribution programs: up to $2,500 per employee per year excluded from income, a separate written plan and nondiscrimination rules. Contributions are permitted from Jul 4, 2026. DOL TR 2026-02 (Jun 17) says they are generally outside ERISA if conditions are met. They are reported on the 2026 W-2 with code TA.

recentChanges.title: EEOC proposes to rescind EEO-1 and all EEO data reports
recentChanges.detail: The Commission voted in July 2026 to propose rescinding EEO-1 through EEO-6 race and sex reporting (comments to Aug 24, 2026; hearing Aug 11). The 2025 EEO-1 collection had not opened as of Sept 2026. Current requirements stay until a final rule, and state reporting (CA, IL, MA) continues.

recentChanges.title: Pay-transparency wave: Virginia, Maine, Connecticut
recentChanges.detail: VA (all employers, Jul 1, 2026) requires ranges in public and internal postings and bans pay-history inquiries. ME (10+ employees, Jul 29, 2026). CT moves from on-request to proactive posting disclosure plus a benefits description on Oct 1, 2026 (all employers). DE follows Sept 26, 2027 (26+ employees).

recentChanges.title: Colorado repeals and replaces its AI Act (SB 26-189)
recentChanges.detail: Signed May 14, 2026 and effective Jan 1, 2027, after a federal court blocked SB 24-205 enforcement (Apr 27, 2026). It replaces risk-assessment and anti-discrimination duties with notice of AI use in consequential decisions, a plain-language explanation within 30 days of adverse decisions, data correction and human review. AG enforcement includes a 60-day cure period.

recentChanges.title: DEI enforcement escalates: first FCA settlement and new contractor EO
recentChanges.detail: DOJ's Civil Rights Fraud Initiative produced a $17M False Claims Act settlement with IBM (Apr 10, 2026) over diverse-slate rules, demographic targets and demographic-linked bonuses. A Mar 26, 2026 EO ('Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors') adds certification, subcontractor monitoring and FCA materiality clauses, building on EO 14173 (Jan 21, 2025), which revoked EO 11246.

recentChanges.title: DOL proposes sharply higher prevailing wage levels (H-1B, E-3, H-1B1, PERM)
recentChanges.detail: NPRM published Mar 31, 2026 (comments closed May 26) would move OEWS wage levels I-IV from the 17th/34th/50th/67th to the 34th/52nd/70th/88th percentiles. A final rule is pending.

recentChanges.title: Washington enacts a full non-compete ban (effective Jun 30, 2027)
recentChanges.detail: ESHB 1155 (signed Mar 23, 2026) voids all employee and contractor non-competes, including existing ones, from Jun 30, 2027. Customer non-solicits are limited to 18 months, and notice to affected current and former workers is due by Oct 1, 2027. Remedies include $5,000 statutory damages plus fees.

recentChanges.title: Wage-weighted H-1B lottery takes effect
recentChanges.detail: DHS final rule (published Dec 29, 2025, effective Feb 27, 2026) weights registrations by OEWS level (IV gets 4 entries, I gets 1) and was used for the March 2026 FY2027 registration. It drew 211,600 registrations (down 38.5%); the cap was reached with no second round, and 71.5% of selected beneficiaries held advanced US degrees.

recentChanges.title: Agency reset: NLRB quorum restored; EEOC rescinds harassment guidance
recentChanges.detail: The NLRB regained a quorum Jan 7, 2026 when Murphy and Mayer were sworn in, along with GC Carey. The EEOC, with a quorum since Oct 2025, rescinded its entire 2024 harassment guidance Jan 22, 2026 (2-1) and now requires Commission approval for new lawsuits.

recentChanges.title: 2026 payroll and benefits changes (OBBBA, SECURE 2.0, state PFML)
recentChanges.detail: From 2026: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed Jul 4, 2025) raises the dependent care FSA cap to $7,500, adds W-2 reporting of qualified overtime and tips (codes TT/TP), raises the 1099 threshold to $2,000 and makes IRC 127 student-loan aid permanent. Mandatory Roth catch-up applies to employees whose prior-year FICA wages exceeded $150K. Other 2026 figures: 401(k) $24,500 and ACA affordability 9.96%. MN and DE PFML benefits began Jan 1; IL AI-in-employment amendments (HB 3773) took effect Jan 1.

watchlist.title: $100K H-1B fee appeals and extended proclamation
watchlist.detail: The government's merits appeal is pending in the 1st Circuit, the Chamber of Commerce case is in the D.C. Circuit, and an emergency Supreme Court application is possible. If the vacatur is stayed or reversed, the fee could apply again immediately to petitions for workers abroad and consular-notification filings through Sept 21, 2027.

watchlist.title: Final rule on the $103,265 cap-subject H-1B fee
watchlist.detail: DHS wants it in place for FY2028 petitions filed from Apr 1, 2027; litigation is likely. Budget for it in FY2028 registrations (March 2027).

watchlist.title: DOL prevailing wage final rule and implementation of the layoffs EO
watchlist.detail: Higher wage floors would affect H-1B, PERM and E-3 costs and weighted-lottery tiers. DOL's 30-day review of prior LCAs under the Sept 18, 2026 EO may trigger audits of employers with recent layoffs.

watchlist.title: NLRB overruling Stericycle, McLaren Macomb, Cemex and Amazon captive-audience
watchlist.detail: The new 3-1 majority needs suitable cases (e.g., Valley Radiology on McLaren). Until then, keep Section 7 carve-outs in handbooks and severance agreements.

watchlist.title: EEOC final rescission of EEO-1; PWFA regulation rewrite
watchlist.detail: A final rule could end EEO-1 filing; the agenda targets an NPRM revising PWFA 'related medical conditions'. The EEOC may also rescind national-origin guidelines and the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (UGESP).

watchlist.title: DOL independent contractor and joint employer rules
watchlist.detail: The Feb 26, 2026 NPRM would restore the 2021 core-factor test. The final rule and related litigation will shape contractor and EOR use.

watchlist.title: 2027 state effective dates
watchlist.detail: CO SB 26-189 AI duties (Jan 1, 2027); MD FAMLI contributions (Jan 1, 2027); IL non-compete salary thresholds rise to $80K and $47.5K (Jan 1, 2027); WA non-compete ban (Jun 30, 2027; notices by Oct 1, 2027); DE pay transparency (Sept 26, 2027).

watchlist.title: First 2026 W-2 cycle with OBBBA codes
watchlist.detail: Codes TT (overtime), TP (tips) and TA (Trump accounts) and Box 14b occupation codes appear on W-2s issued Jan 2027. Final Trump-account regulations are also pending (hearing Oct 15, 2026).

calendar.title: W-2/W-3 and 1099-NEC due Jan 31
calendar.detail: Furnish to employees and file with SSA/IRS by Jan 31. The 2026 W-2s (issued Jan 2027) include the new TT/TP/TA codes. Also due: Form 941 (Q4) and 940 (FUTA) by Jan 31. Jan 1 brings new state minimum wages, exempt thresholds and PFML/UI rates.

calendar.title: OSHA 300A posting and MA demographic report
calendar.detail: Post the certified 300A summary from Feb 1 to Apr 30 at each establishment. The MA workforce demographic report (100+ MA employees) is due Feb 1. Employees claiming W-4 exemption must renew by Feb 15.

calendar.title: OSHA ITA e-submission and 1095-C furnishing (about Mar 2)
calendar.detail: Submit 300A data (and 300/301 for Appendix B establishments) by Mar 2. Furnish Forms 1095-C by the automatic 30-day extension date (about Mar 2).

calendar.title: H-1B cap registration (FY+1)
calendar.detail: The USCIS electronic registration window is usually in March ($215 per registration). The wage-weighted lottery requires the correct OEWS level. Prepare the candidate list in January-February.

calendar.title: ACA e-filing due Mar 31
calendar.detail: File Forms 1094-C/1095-C electronically with the IRS by Mar 31. Some states (CA, NJ, MA, RI, DC) have individual-mandate reporting with different deadlines.

calendar.title: H-1B cap petitions: Apr 1 - Jun 30 window
calendar.detail: File selected cap petitions within the 90-day window. Check the status of the $100K fee and any new cap fee before filing consular-notification cases.

calendar.title: RxDC reporting (Jun 1) and historical EEO-1 window
calendar.detail: Prescription drug data collection for group health plans is due Jun 1. The EEO-1 historically ran May-June; the 2025 collection had not opened as of Sept 2026 and rescission is proposed.

calendar.title: Form 5500 and PCORI fee due Jul 31
calendar.detail: Calendar-year plans file Form 5500 by Jul 31 (Form 5558 extends to Oct 15). PCORI fee (Form 720) is due for self-insured plans. Form 941 (Q2) is also due.

calendar.title: VETS-4212 due Sept 30 (federal contractors)
calendar.detail: The filing window runs Aug 1 - Sept 30. Also review annual VEVRAA and Section 503 AAPs; EO 11246 AAPs are no longer required.

calendar.title: H-1B cap start date and Medicare Part D notice
calendar.detail: H-1B cap employment starts Oct 1 (cap-gap ends). Send the Medicare Part D creditable coverage notice by Oct 15. Extended Form 5500 filings are due Oct 15.

calendar.title: Open enrollment
calendar.detail: Distribute the SBC and annual notices, set next year's contributions against the ACA affordability percentage, update HSA/FSA/DCAP elections to the new limits, and confirm Roth catch-up coding for employees with prior-year FICA wages over the threshold.

calendar.title: Year-end compliance refresh
calendar.detail: Update handbook state addenda, pay ranges, minimum wage and exempt salary changes for Jan 1, new state leave notices, and NY/IL annual harassment training completion. Test payroll for W-2 code readiness.

gotchas: Treating remote employees as if they work at HQ: the work state (and city) governs payroll registration, minimum wage, overtime, PFML and sick leave, final pay, non-competes, WARN counting and notices. Hiring into a new state without registering and issuing state notices is the most common multi-state error.

Posting 'remote - US' roles without a pay range: CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, NJ, VT, MA and others can reach remote roles that may be filled in-state, and VA, ME and CT joined in 2026. The safest practice is a good-faith range plus a benefits summary on every US posting and internal promotion notice.

Assuming federal changes are settled law: the EEO-1 is still on the books while rescission is pending, and the NLRB has signaled change but Stericycle and McLaren Macomb remain binding. The $100K H-1B fee is vacated but was re-proclaimed, and could return overnight if a stay is granted.

Using template severance agreements with blanket confidentiality or non-disparagement and no carve-outs for Section 7, SEC or EEOC reporting and the Speak Out Act. Omitting OWBPA group disclosures in RIFs voids ADEA releases.

Relying on $684/week as the exempt test everywhere: state thresholds are far higher (CA, NY, WA, CO), and junior engineers or lab technicians who fail the duties test need overtime. Qualified overtime must now be tracked for W-2 reporting.

Running DEI programs with demographic eligibility, diverse-slate mandates or diversity-linked bonuses. For a company with federal contracts or grants this creates False Claims Act exposure (the IBM $17M settlement), and after Ames any employee can bring Title VII claims.

Treating I-9 errors as fixable later: ICE's Mar 2026 guidance makes many former technical errors substantive with no cure period. Using remote I-9 review without E-Verify good standing, or demanding specific documents, adds penalties.

Mixing export-control screening with I-9 or asking all candidates about citizenship: this invites DOJ IER citizenship and document-abuse charges. Use a separate, narrow, uniformly applied export-control question only for roles with controlled-technology access.

Planning a RIF without state mini-WARN review (NY 90 days at 50+ employees; NJ 90 days plus mandatory severance, counting employees who report to NJ sites) or without checking H-1B effects (bona fide termination steps; layoffs now weighed in H-1B adjudication).

Keeping or threatening to enforce non-competes where they are void (MN, WY, ND, OK, CA; WA from Jun 2027). This can bring statutory damages, fee shifting and FTC Section 5 attention; rely on NDAs, IP assignment and narrow non-solicits instead.
semiconductorNotes: I-9 and deemed exports are separate processes. The I-9 confirms work authorization only. EAR/ITAR deemed-export screening (whether a foreign national's access to controlled chip design or process technology needs a license) must run as a separate, uniformly applied, need-based process to avoid 8 U.S.C. 1324b citizenship discrimination. Form I-129 Part 6 requires a deemed-export attestation for H-1B/L-1/O-1 petitions (details are in the export-control file).

Trade secrets: engineers are the main exfiltration risk. Put the DTSA immunity notice in every confidentiality/PIIA (otherwise exemplary damages and fees against that individual are lost), monitor pre-departure downloads, image devices and use exit certifications. As non-competes shrink (MN, WY, WA from 2027), protection shifts to NDAs, invention assignment with state carve-outs and narrow non-solicits.

Visa-heavy engineering teams: the wage-weighted H-1B lottery favors high-paid semiconductor roles, but the proposed prevailing wage increase, the proposed $103,265 cap fee and the layoffs EO raise cost and scrutiny. Coordinate RIF timing with pending LCAs and petitions, and consider O-1 and L-1 routes for senior talent and cross-border transfers.

Lab safety at a fabless company: characterization, failure-analysis, reliability, RF and photonics labs bring the OSHA Lab Standard (Chemical Hygiene Plan), HazCom 2024 updates, laser, X-ray and ESD programs and electrical safety for high-voltage benches. Non-exempt lab technicians on shifts need overtime and on-call pay practices.

Equity-heavy pay: RSU and ESPP programs drive supplemental withholding (22% or 37% over $1M), multi-state sourcing for mobile employees, Nasdaq clawback (Rule 5608) and insider-trading blackout administration. Severance and RIF packages should specify vesting treatment clearly.

CHIPS Act: workforce, childcare and reporting commitments bind only direct award recipients and follow the specific award terms, which Commerce revisited in 2025-26 (verify current conditions). The 48D investment tax credit by itself imposes no HR conditions. Fabless firms usually have no CHIPS workforce obligations unless they received a grant.

Federal contracts (e.g., defense or aerospace chip programs) trigger VEVRAA/Section 503 AAPs, the EO 14173 and Mar 2026 DEI certifications with FCA exposure, the E-Verify FAR clause and, for classified work, NISPOM insider-threat and security-clearance HR processes.

Remote chip designers spread across many states multiply exposure: IL BIPA if biometric lab access is used, NY/CT/DE monitoring notices for security tooling, and AI screening rules (NYC LL 144, IL HB 3773, CO from 2027) for high-volume new-graduate hiring.
